notes: Gross pay for the loads. Book the full amount even though deductions come out before the deposit
Billed to the shipper, so it is revenue. Some bookkeepers use a separate Fuel surcharge revenue line to compare it with fuel cost
Detention, layover, stop-off and lumper reimbursements paid by the carrier
Fuel bought on the carrier's card. Do not book the same fill again from the fuel card statement
Cargo, liability, bobtail or physical damage premiums the carrier deducts
An asset, not an expense. The carrier holds it and pays it back when the lease ends, less any charges
Money set aside by the carrier for repairs. Also an asset until it is spent
Weekly set-aside for the heavy vehicle use tax. An asset until the tax is paid
Tolls and scale tickets charged back by the carrier
Plate or permit program charged back in weekly instalments
Trailer rent charged by the carrier
Cash advanced to the driver. Usually a draw, but if it paid a business cost the receipt decides the account
Lease-purchase or truck note taken through the settlement. Split it: interest to expense, principal against the loan
